summary: Search for investment-based residence or citizenship routes in Europe, the Middle East and Central Asia not yet in programs.csv. Four programmes added, each from stored official texts: San Marino elective residence (EUR 500,000 home or EUR 600,000 ten-year state-securities deposit, since 2017), Kazakhstan's AIFC Investment Tax Residency Programme (USD 60,000, since 2022), the Isle of Man's Tier 1 (Investor) route (GBP 1 million, GBP 2 million from Nov 2014; closed Feb 2022), and Serbia's residence for property owners (no minimum value, in scope under decision 15 refined). Albanian and Turkish property and investor grounds were found too but are already proposed by the extract-partials passes; only the Turkish implementing regulation is added here. No counts were found for any of them. Many other candidates were out of scope (Austria, Poland, the previously reviewed Czech, Romanian, German and Kuwaiti routes, Albania's investor permit) or could not be checked because the session's web search budget was used up; see gaps.

sources.title: Zakon o strancima (Sl. glasnik RS, br. 97/08)
sources.covers: Serbia's 2008 Law on Foreigners, in force eight days after publication and applied from 1 April 2009. Art. 26 lists the purposes of temporary residence (work, study, family reunion, other justified reasons); there is no ground based on owning property.
sources.notes: Copy retrieved from the Wayback Machine (capture of 22 Dec 2009). Header dates the text 23.10.2008, Sl. glasnik 97/08. Used only to show that the property-ownership ground was new in the 2018 law.

sources.title: Yabancılar ve Uluslararası Koruma Kanununun Uygulanmasına İlişkin Yönetmelik (RG 17.03.2016, sayı 29656), güncel metin
sources.covers: Implementing regulation of Law 6458. Art. 28(3): residence applications by property owners require the property to be a dwelling used as such; family members who co-own it may also apply.
sources.notes: Consolidated text as served on 11 Oct 2026. No property value threshold appears in it; the Ministry's value decision under art. 31(6) of the law (added 2024) was not found.

sources.title: Testo coordinato Legge 28 giugno 2010 n.118 - Legge sull'ingresso e la permanenza degli stranieri in Repubblica (aggiornato al 3 giugno 2025)
sources.publisher: Consiglio Grande e Generale, Repubblica di San Marino
sources.covers: Coordinated text of San Marino's law on foreigners with all amendments to 3 June 2025, with the original wording of amended articles in footnotes. Art. 16-bis 'residenza elettiva' (introduced by Legge 94/2017): purchase of a home for at least EUR 500,000 or a 10-year non-interest-bearing deposit of at least EUR 600,000 in San Marino state securities or a state fund; EUR 10,000 tax for the deposit route; EUR 1,000 application charge; EUR 20,000 per added family member; cap of 50 a year; residence consolidated after 10 years. Also art. 16-ter (flat-tax 'residenza atipica' for people with foreign income) and 16-quater (pensioners: income and bank assets).
sources.notes: Downloaded as a zip from the Council's coordinated-texts index ('Residenze e permessi di soggiorno'); the stored file is the version with notes. The page numbers cited are those printed at the foot of each page.

sources.title: Legge 7 agosto 2017 n.94 - Variazione al Bilancio di Previsione dello Stato ... per l'esercizio finanziario 2017
sources.publisher: Consiglio Grande e Generale, Repubblica di San Marino

programs.name: Serbia temporary residence on the basis of property ownership (Law on Foreigners, art. 40(1)(10) and art. 54)
programs.notes: Out of scope (METHODOLOGY decision 18): owning a home with no minimum value is a general rule for property owners, not a route that is sold. Rows kept, not shown. Temporary residence for a foreigner who owns a residential building or flat in Serbia in which he or she lives, on proof of ownership and the general conditions of art. 43 (means, insurance, no bar). The law sets no minimum value. Under decision 15 (refined), buying property counts even without a minimum price. The ground was introduced by the Law on Foreigners of 2018 (Sl. glasnik RS 24/2018), which enters into force eight days after publication and applies six months after entry into force; the exact publication and application dates were not read, so launched is empty. The 2008 law (97/08) had no property ground. Permit length, renewal and any path to permanent residence or citizenship were not researched. The only copy of the current text read is a commercial database consolidation (Paragraf, to 62/2023); the official portal (pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs) is script-rendered and was not read. No counts found.

programs.name: San Marino elective residence (residenza elettiva, Law 118/2010 art. 16-bis)
programs.notes: The Congress of State may grant 'elective residence' to a foreigner who makes and keeps in his or her own name, until the residence is consolidated, one or both of: buying a home for at least EUR 500,000 (up to EUR 150,000 of completion, renovation or rebuilding costs may count) or a 10-year non-interest-bearing tied deposit of at least EUR 600,000 in San Marino state securities or a fund set up by the state. The deposit route also carries a non-refundable tax of EUR 10,000; every application pays EUR 1,000; each family member added pays EUR 20,000 once. Holders may not work in the public sector, get no residence-linked benefits and must insure their own health care until the residence is consolidated after ten years. At most 50 grants a year (excluding family members). Introduced by art. 19 of Law 94 of 7 August 2017 (in force on the fifth day after legal publication; the publication date is not printed, so launched is the law's date). The 2017 text limited the property route to buildings completed, unfinished or to be renovated before 31 May 2017; Law 183 of 29 October 2021 removed that date. The flat-tax residence for people with foreign income (art. 16-ter) and the pensioners' residence (art. 16-quater, income and bank assets) are income-based and out of scope (decision 15). No counts of elective residences were found (the Foreign Secretary reports to a Council commission; those reports were not searched).

programs.name: Kazakhstan AIFC Investment Tax Residency Programme (Astana International Financial Centre)
programs.notes: Run by the Astana International Financial Centre under art. 5-1 of the Constitutional Statute on the AIFC. A foreigner who invests at least USD 60,000 (or equivalent) in eligible instruments (shares or units of AIFC funds or entities, securities listed on the Astana International Exchange, capital of an AIFC-registered entity; from 2026 also digital assets on AFSA-licensed platforms, minimum USD 150,000) receives an Investment Resident Certificate for up to five years and, on the AIFC's request, an investor visa or a temporary residence permit for himself or herself and family under Kazakh migration law, plus tax benefits. The Kazakh government's immigrant rules provide temporary residence for AIFC investment residents for one year, renewable up to five years, and investor visas of up to five years (para. 19-1 added in March 2021, before this programme, so an earlier AIFC investment-residence status existed; its rules were not found). Launched 2022-09-14: date the 2022 Regulations (No. 42) were enacted; they commence on publication on the AIFC website, a date not printed. Replaced by Regulations No. 57 of 6 August 2026 and Rules No. 5 (commencing 6 August 2026), which keep USD 60,000, add the digital-asset option and require three full-time jobs for Kazakh citizens on the share-capital option. Fees: USD 7,750 (main applicant) in the 2024 fee table; at least USD 8,990 including taxes under the 2026 rules. Separate from the government investor visa for USD 300,000 introduced in 2025 (kaz-investor-visa, proposed by the leads-africa-asia-americas pass). No counts found.

programs.name: Isle of Man Tier 1 (Investor) Migrant route (Isle of Man Immigration Rules)
programs.notes: The Isle of Man's own version of the UK Tier 1 (Investor) route, for high net worth individuals investing in the Isle of Man. Entry needed GBP 1 million of the applicant's own money disposable in the Isle of Man (or personal assets over GBP 2 million plus GBP 1 million borrowed from a regulated institution); from 10 November 2014 GBP 2 million of own money, invested in share or loan capital of active and trading Isle of Man companies. Settlement after 5 years at GBP 2 million, 3 years at GBP 5 million or 2 years at GBP 10 million (from 2014). The route is in the December 2009 consolidated rules (earliest version found), so launched is empty: the Statement of Changes that introduced it was not retrieved. Closed to new applicants from the rules in effect 23 February 2022; the version in effect 14-22 February 2022 still allowed entry clearance, so 'ended' is 22 February 2022 (any transitional rule for pending applications was not read). Before Tier 1 the rules had an 'investor' category (paras 224-231: GBP 1 million, GBP 750,000 to invest), still in the 2009 text; not recorded separately (its start and end were not established). Jersey and Guernsey had equivalent categories (the Isle of Man rules count time spent in them); not researched. No counts found.

events.title: Serbia's new Law on Foreigners adds temporary residence on the basis of property ownership
events.description: The Law on Foreigners published in Sl. glasnik RS 24/2018 lists ownership of real property as a ground for temporary residence (art. 40(1)(10), art. 54). It enters into force eight days after publication and applies six months after entry into force; exact dates not read. The 2008 law had no such ground.

events.title: San Marino creates elective residence for EUR 500,000 property or EUR 600,000 state-securities deposit
events.description: Art. 19 of Law 94 of 7 August 2017 inserts art. 16-bis into Law 118/2010: elective residence for a home purchase of at least EUR 500,000 or a 10-year deposit of at least EUR 600,000 in state securities; 50 grants for 2017. The law enters into force on the fifth day after legal publication (date not printed), so the date is the law's date.
events.quote: La presente legge entra in vigore il quinto giorno successivo a quello della sua legale

events.title: San Marino fixes the elective-residence cap at 50 a year
events.description: Decreto Delegato 75 of 8 May 2020 replaces art. 16-bis(15): at most 50 elective residences a year, family members excluded (the 2017 text set 50 for 2017 and left later years to a decree). Date is the decree's date; in-force date not read.
events.quote: Il numero massimo di residenze elettive che possono essere concesse ogni anno è di 50 unità, esclusi i casi di cui ai commi 6 e 7.

events.title: San Marino opens the elective-residence property route to buildings of any date
events.description: Law 183 of 29 October 2021, art. 16, rewrites art. 16-bis(1)(a), dropping the requirement that the building be completed, unfinished or to be renovated before 31 May 2017. Date is the law's date; in-force date not read.
events.quote: Legge 29 ottobre 2021 n.183 Art.16 (Modifica articolo 16-bis della Legge 28 giugno 2010 n.118 e sue successive modifiche – Residenza elettiva)

events.title: AIFC enacts its Investment Tax Residency Programme regulations (USD 60,000)
events.description: AIFC Regulations No. 42 of 2022 create the Investment Tax Residency Programme: USD 60,000 in eligible AIFC instruments gives an Investment Resident Certificate for up to five years and access to an investor visa or temporary residence permit. Enacted on adoption by the Governor; commence on publication on the AIFC website (date not printed).

events.title: AIFC replaces the investment residency regulations: digital-asset option at USD 150,000, job condition on company capital
events.description: AIFC Regulations No. 57 of 2026 (6 August 2026) replace No. 42; Rules No. 5 commence 6 August 2026. The USD 60,000 minimum must be maintained at all times; digital assets on AFSA-licensed platforms added at USD 150,000; the share-capital option requires three full-time jobs for Kazakh citizens; total fee at least USD 8,990.
events.quote: upon such commencement, AIFC Regulations on AIFC Investment Tax Residency Programme No. 42 shall cease to have effect.

events.title: Tier 1 (Investor) route in the Isle of Man Immigration Rules (December 2009)
events.description: Earliest consolidated Isle of Man rules found: Tier 1 (Investor) Migrants (paras 245O-245U), GBP 1 million. When the route was introduced was not established.
events.quote: This route is for high net worth individuals making a substantial financial investment to the Isle of Man.

events.title: Isle of Man doubles the Tier 1 (Investor) threshold to GBP 2 million
events.description: Statement of Changes SD 2014/0344 (laid 9 Dec 2014, effective 10 Nov 2014): GBP 2 million of own money required; accelerated settlement tiers; applications made before 10 November 2014 decided under the old rules.
events.quote: The changes in this Statement shall take effect on 10th November 2014.

events.title: Isle of Man closes the Tier 1 (Investor) route to new applicants
events.description: From the Immigration Rules in effect 23 February 2022, para 245E says the route is closed to new applicants; existing holders may extend or settle. The rules in effect 14-22 February 2022 still provided for entry clearance. The Statement of Changes making the closure was not retrieved.
events.quote: This route is now closed to new applicants. Individuals who already have entry clearance, leave to enter or remain as a Tier 1 (Investor) Migrant may apply under these rules to extend their stay or for indefinite leave to remain.

Austria: the private-means settlement permit (NAG § 44, 'Niederlassungsbewilligung - ausgenommen Erwerbstätigkeit') needs fixed regular monthly income of twice the ASVG reference rates and a quota place: an income test, out of scope (decision 15). Stored: aut-ris-nag-2026. The self-employed key worker (AuslBG § 24(1)) names EUR 100,000 of investment capital only as one way to show macroeconomic benefit of a self-employment; treated as out of scope like Germany's § 21 presumption (decision 15 refined). Stored: aut-ris-auslbg-2026. A person may want to confirm this judgement.

The in-force dates of Law 94/2017, DD 75/2020 and Law 183/2021 are not printed in the texts read. Art. 16-ter (flat tax of 7% on foreign income, minimum EUR 10,000 a year) and 16-quater (pensioners: EUR 120,000 income and EUR 300,000 bank assets) were judged income-based and out of scope (decision 15), though 16-ter resembles Switzerland's lump-sum taxation, which is in the data.

Serbia: the official text of the 2018 Law on Foreigners and its publication date (Sl. glasnik RS 24/2018) were not obtained (pravno-informacioni-sistem.rs is script-rendered; Wayback was intermittently offline).
